operationalization: Code tissue samples and anatomical structures by whether repeated subdivision preserves tissue identity; test whether every animal part fits one of the two classes.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: anatomical entities and part relationships across taxa

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen anatomy for checking composite structures

obstacles: “Part” and “like itself” require scale-dependent interpretation.
rationale: Ontologies and specimen images permit tests of selected structures, but the proposed dichotomy is partly conceptual and changes with spatial scale.

operationalization: Choose explicit criteria for correspondence, such as developmental origin, position or function, then compare each named pair across taxa.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: homology and phenotype annotations for vertebrate structures

obstacles: Analogy has several non-equivalent modern meanings.
rationale: Comparative data exist, but no observation alone decides Aristotle’s intended relation without first imposing a modern correspondence criterion.

operationalization: Map oistros to candidate insect taxa and compare documented larval habitat and metamorphosis; aquatic larvae yielding the adult would support the account.

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: occurrences for candidate insect taxa and life stages

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public life-history accounts for candidate taxa

obstacles: The identity of oistros is uncertain.
Larval-stage records are sparse.
rationale: The life cycle is directly testable for a mapped species, but taxonomic ambiguity and scattered developmental records prevent resolving the statement as stated.

operationalization: Classify raptor species by hooked talons and flocking outside breeding, then test whether any species regularly forms flocks.

candidate_datasets.name: EltonTraits 1.0
candidate_datasets.role: foraging and social ecology traits for birds

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: large occurrence samples usable to detect aggregation

obstacles: “Gregarious” needs a frequency and season threshold.
rationale: Standardized bird traits and occurrence records cover most raptors. A documented regularly flocking hooked-taloned species would cleanly refute the universal.

operationalization: Enumerate domesticated animal lineages and determine whether extant or historical free-living wild progenitor populations exist for each.
obstacles: Feral populations are not necessarily wild progenitors.
“Same kind” may mean species or domestic lineage.
rationale: The named domesticates and their progenitors are extensively documented. Defining wild as ancestral rather than feral makes a tractable lineage-by-lineage test.

operationalization: Across coded animal taxa, record presence of urinary bladder and intestine and test whether bladder presence ever occurs without an intestine.
obstacles: Bladder homologues differ among major clades.
Coverage is incomplete outside vertebrates.
rationale: The implication has a clear counterexample criterion, but no single open matrix adequately samples all animals and homologizes every excretory organ.

operationalization: Define touch as mechanosensory response and survey experimentally documented sensory modalities across animal phyla; any animal lacking mechanosensation refutes universality.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: taxon accounts and links to sensory biology literature

obstacles: Animal and sense boundaries are theory-laden.
No comprehensive cross-phyla sensory dataset.
rationale: A measurable proxy exists, but evidence is dispersed and especially weak for microscopic and poorly studied phyla, limiting a universal conclusion.

operationalization: Map bloodless to absence of vertebrate red blood and count locomotory appendages by species; search for blooded species with more than four feet or bloodless exceptions.
obstacles: “Feet” excludes or includes different appendage types.
Ancient “bloodless” is not exactly invertebrate.
rationale: With explicit mappings, anatomy databases sample the relevant clades and counterexamples are decisive. Remaining uncertainty is primarily terminological.

operationalization: Use embryological observations to track which egg compartments become embryo versus extraembryonic nutrition and compare that pattern with insect larval metamorphosis.
obstacles: Egg organization varies greatly among clades.
rationale: Embryonic fate and yolk use are standard observable variables with abundant published records, although a broad all-ovipara comparison requires harmonization.

operationalization: Code reproductive mode in shark species as oviparity, ovoviviparity or placental viviparity and test for embryos developing from retained eggs.
obstacles: “Sharks” may include rays in the ancient grouping.
rationale: Open species accounts and fish trait records directly document internal egg retention and live birth, allowing a decisive taxon-by-taxon test.

operationalization: For invertebrate species, model maximum adult body mass against marine versus freshwater or terrestrial habitat and climatic temperature.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: marine invertebrate size and habitat traits

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: geographic occurrences for deriving climate exposure

obstacles: Maximum size is missing for many invertebrates.
Sampling and discovery bias favor large marine species.
rationale: Size, habitat and climate can be joined for substantial subsets, but taxonomic gaps and correlated sampling biases prevent a full-scope test.

operationalization: Identify hair-bearing species and code reproductive mode; any egg-laying hair-bearing species refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts including integument and reproduction

obstacles: Whether monotreme pelage counts as a coat needs explicit coding.
rationale: These are standard mammalian traits with near-complete coverage, and monotremes provide a direct discriminating case.

operationalization: Count and map cranial sutures on sex-labelled adult human CT scans or skull specimens and compare distributions between sexes.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D human crania where access and metadata permit

obstacles: Age and suture fusion confound sex comparisons.
Some collections restrict sensitive human specimens.
rationale: The anatomical variables are direct and large imaging collections exist. Age-adjusted segmentation would clearly test the claimed sex-specific patterns.

operationalization: Inspect external and internal ocular anatomy in mapped Talpa and Spalax specimens and compare visual capability and eye presence with other viviparous mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D cranial specimens of moles and mole-rats

obstacles: The ancient animal may map to Talpa or Spalax.
Behavioral blindness is distinct from reduced eyes.
rationale: Imaging can directly reveal reduced eyes under skin for both candidate taxa. The uniqueness clause is broader and somewhat less well covered.

operationalization: Compile within-species iris-colour polymorphism for humans, horses and other animals and compare the prevalence of multiple stable colours.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts that may document eye-colour variation

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public taxon descriptions and linked literature

obstacles: No comprehensive cross-species iris-colour dataset.
Colour categories and age effects need standardization.
rationale: The claim has a clear comparative variable, but observations are scattered and biased toward domestic and charismatic species.

operationalization: Trace anatomical lumens from the middle ear toward the nasopharynx and brain on CT/MRI and dissection records across ear-bearing taxa.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: human head imaging for ear and cranial connections

obstacles: “Inner cavity” likely refers to the middle rather than inner ear.
rationale: Modern imaging directly resolves the Eustachian connection and absence of an open conduit to brain; terminology is the main interpretive issue.

operationalization: Code voluntary pinna movement in mammals and test whether any nonhuman ear-bearing species lacks it or any human displays functional movement.
obstacles: Movement may mean voluntary, reflexive or muscular capacity.
Behavior is not systematically coded across mammals.
rationale: The test is simple for sampled mammals, but open trait databases do not comprehensively encode pinna mobility and rare variation complicates universality.

operationalization: Quantify upper- and lower-jaw motion relative to the skull from crocodile and comparative feeding kinematics; test whether the upper jaw alone moves.

candidate_datasets.name: Digital Morphology
candidate_datasets.role: crocodilian skull anatomy and comparative imaging

obstacles: Apparent upper-jaw motion can result from head elevation.
rationale: Anatomy and kinematic literature can directly distinguish jaw rotation from whole-head movement, making the claim decisively testable.

operationalization: Count rib pairs on adult human CT scans and estimate the population distribution; counts other than eight refute the statement.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public thoracic CT scans showing rib counts

obstacles: Rare congenital rib-number variants require representative sampling.
rationale: Ribs are unambiguous on abundant open CT imaging, and the numerical prediction has a direct decisive test.

operationalization: Fit phylogenetic models of brain mass versus body mass across animals, and separately compare standardized brain water fraction.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: mammal body-size traits for joining to brain datasets

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: body mass and taxonomic metadata across animals

obstacles: Brain water content lacks broad comparable coverage.
“Moistest” has no specified measurement protocol.
rationale: Relative brain size is resolvable for many vertebrates, but comparable water-content data are sparse, so only part of the conjunction can be tested.

operationalization: Measure cerebral vessels, perfused blood volume and tissue temperature in anatomical or imaging datasets across representative vertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: vascular and perfusion imaging of human brains

obstacles: Coldness depends on measurement conditions.
Cross-taxon perfusion and temperature data are not harmonized.
rationale: The vascular assertions are directly testable and richly documented for some taxa, while the universal and thermal components lack adequate open coverage.

operationalization: Segment heart chambers in human and large-vertebrate imaging, count them and compare chamber volumes.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public cardiac CT and MRI collections

obstacles: Ancient cavity names may not map one-to-one to modern chambers.
rationale: Open imaging and basic anatomy directly expose chamber number and size, providing a strong test after documenting the historical mapping.

operationalization: Compare vascular density or blood-volume fraction among organs of viviparous lung-bearing species using histology and imaging.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: contrast imaging usable for human organ vascularity

obstacles: “Most richly supplied” needs a normalized vascularity metric.
Cross-organ, cross-species protocols differ.
rationale: Vascularity can be quantified in selected mammals, but no harmonized open dataset supports the full taxonomic superlative.

operationalization: Measure cranio-caudal positions of left and right kidneys in images from diverse kidney-bearing species and search for reversals.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: human and veterinary-style anatomical imaging collections

obstacles: Body orientation differs among taxa.
Open soft-tissue coverage is uneven outside mammals.
rationale: The positional relation is simple and well documented for many clades; broad imaging can reveal counterexamples, though all-animal coverage is incomplete.

operationalization: Count cervical vertebrae in lion skeletons or CT volumes; more than one neck bone refutes the statement.
rationale: The numerical anatomical claim can be checked directly on public specimens with no specialized inference.

operationalization: Classify posture during sleep from tagged video or behavioral records of captive and wild elephants and estimate the frequency of standing versus lateral sleep.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: elephant behavior accounts and linked sources

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence and observation links that may include behavior

obstacles: Sleep posture is rarely standardized in public occurrence data.
Captivity and age affect posture.
rationale: Existing observations can test elephants in several settings, but no broad open sleep-posture dataset covers populations and contexts adequately.

operationalization: Join horn presence and number to foot morphology across terrestrial mammals and search for a two-horned solid-hoofed species.
obstacles: Horn must be distinguished from antler and ossicone.
rationale: The relevant mammalian structures are well catalogued, and a single correctly coded equid-like counterexample would be decisive.

operationalization: Code annual shedding and regrowth of cranial appendages across horned mammals and model age at first shedding in cervids.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: mammal species accounts with antler biology

obstacles: “Deer” could mean one species or Cervidae.
Age at first shedding varies by species and condition.
rationale: Comparative accounts clearly distinguish annually shed antlers from permanent horns, with sufficient species coverage to test both uniqueness and timing.

operationalization: Inspect male reproductive skeletons for an ossified baculum in fox, wolf, marten and weasel specimens.
obstacles: Species and sex metadata must be verified.
rationale: Bacula are discrete skeletal structures and public museum imaging can resolve their presence in each named taxon.

operationalization: Code tusks, paired horns and interlocking pointed dentition across mammals; search for co-occurrence in any species.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: comparative dental and cranial character matrices

obstacles: Tusks and saw-teeth require operational definitions.
Extinct taxa substantially expand the scope.
rationale: The combinations are measurable and extant mammals are tractable, but terminology and incomplete extinct-taxon coding limit the universal.

operationalization: Use age-series dental specimens to identify replacement of premolars/molars and any deciduous-to-permanent tooth replacement in pigs.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: age-series mammalian jaw and tooth specimens

obstacles: Ancient “molar” may include modern premolars.
rationale: Dental eruption and replacement leave clear specimen evidence. With historical tooth terminology mapped, datasets can decisively identify counterexamples.

operationalization: Measure calibrated tooth colour by age in multiple mammal species, including horses, and estimate within-species age trends.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: age-labelled dental specimens potentially usable for imaging

obstacles: No standardized open cross-species tooth-colour dataset.
Diet, wear and preservation alter colour.
rationale: The hypothesis is measurable, but specimen images are not calibrated for colour and age metadata are inconsistent; a targeted standardized dataset is needed.

operationalization: Count permanent teeth in sex-labelled adult human, sheep, goat and pig specimens and compare sex-specific distributions within each species.
obstacles: Missing teeth must be separated from congenital tooth count.
rationale: Sex and tooth counts are standard specimen variables, and adequate imaging can directly test all four named taxa.

operationalization: Across species with adult tooth counts and longevity, fit phylogenetically controlled models of lifespan against tooth number and spacing.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

obstacles: Body size and phylogeny strongly confound the association.
Tooth spacing is not broadly standardized.
rationale: Longevity and tooth-count data overlap for many vertebrates, but the general scope and heavy ecological confounding weaken discrimination.

operationalization: Code pinnae, mammary glands, intromittent organs and testis position in lizards, crocodilians, turtles and frogs; identify any counterexample to each universal.
obstacles: “Copulatory organ” differs homologously among clades.
Sex-specific structures need male specimens.
rationale: These are conspicuous anatomical characters with broad comparative documentation, though combining all four traits requires harmonization.

operationalization: Use time-stamped GPS or accelerometer locations to compare Nile crocodile land occupancy by day and water occupancy by night.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species behavior accounts and source links

obstacles: Occurrence records rarely encode land-versus-water position precisely.
Season and temperature alter haul-out behavior.
rationale: The prediction is clear, but public telemetry is scattered and opportunistic observations are biased, supporting only localized tests.

operationalization: For nights with crocodile telemetry, compare water and air temperature and model transitions into water as a function of their difference.

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: locations for linking observations to environmental temperature

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: crocodile thermoregulation accounts and linked studies

obstacles: Behavior and temperature must be recorded simultaneously.
Other drivers can produce the same movement.
rationale: Existing telemetry and weather data could test some populations, but open paired records are sparse and causal attribution remains confounded.

operationalization: Synchronize chameleon body-volume or respiratory state with calibrated colour video and test whether inflation precedes the stated colour transitions.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: chameleon physiology accounts and linked experimental literature

obstacles: No known open dataset pairs inflation and full-body colour.
Stress, temperature and social context confound colour.
rationale: The temporal mechanism is experimentally measurable, but public reusable observations appear scattered and insufficient for the full causal claim.

operationalization: Define high flight using altitude records, join species to toe arrangement, and test whether all high-fliers have four toes and the stated orientations.
obstacles: AVONET does not directly encode flight altitude or toe orientation.
“Fly high” lacks a threshold.
rationale: Bird morphology has broad open coverage, but flight height and toe arrangement require supplementary sources and interpretation.

operationalization: Code neck, paired limbs, testes and mammary glands across modern fishes, explicitly distinguishing fins and internal gonads.
obstacles: Ancient “limb” and “testicle” do not map cleanly to modern terms.
rationale: Fish anatomy databases provide broad coverage and direct counterexamples for several components; explicit terminology mapping enables a decisive test.

operationalization: Inspect female delphinid specimens and reproductive anatomy records for mammary slits, gland number, location and milk delivery.
obstacles: Soft mammary tissue is absent from many skeletal collections.
rationale: The external slits and mammary anatomy are directly documented across delphinids, so the named anatomical prediction is readily testable.

operationalization: Inspect fish auditory and olfactory anatomy and sensory-response datasets for internal ears, nares and associated passages.
obstacles: External openings must not be conflated with sensory organs.
rationale: Modern anatomical data directly document fish ears and olfactory systems; their presence provides decisive counterevidence.

operationalization: Code reproductive mode across bony and cartilaginous fishes and test each universal plus the anglerfish exception.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: marine species reproductive traits and accounts

obstacles: Ancient scaly/cartilaginous categories need taxonomic mapping.
rationale: FishBase has broad, direct reproductive records, and numerous species-level outcomes can clearly confirm or refute each clause.

operationalization: Examine age-labelled cattle and horse hearts for an os cordis and estimate prevalence by species, breed and age.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: anatomical specimens where soft-tissue metadata exist

obstacles: Open heart specimens are sparse.
Cardiac cartilage may ossify with age.
rationale: The structure is discrete and documented, but reusable specimen-level prevalence data are limited, especially for the qualified cattle statement.

operationalization: Inspect biliary anatomy by species and code gallbladder presence in each named mammal, including variation among pigs.
obstacles: Mule anatomy is inherited and less often represented.
Pig “kinds” requires breed-level data.
rationale: Gallbladder presence is a standard anatomical character with extensive named-taxon documentation; the broad list is directly checkable.

operationalization: Necropsy red deer heads across regions and seasons, identify botfly larvae, and estimate prevalence and count distribution.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: red deer and parasite accounts with literature links

obstacles: Parasite absence is hard to infer without systematic necropsy.
Prevalence varies geographically and seasonally.
rationale: Existing parasite records can refute the exceptionless and fixed-count wording, but they do not form a representative open necropsy dataset.

operationalization: Code kidneys and urinary bladders from bird and fish anatomy across clades; any documented organ presence refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: vertebrate kidney and bladder phenotype annotations

obstacles: Urinary bladder and cloacal storage must be distinguished.
rationale: Comparative anatomy directly records these organs over broad samples, and counterexamples are anatomically unambiguous after terminology is fixed.

operationalization: Across horned ungulates, jointly code upper incisors, stomach chamber count and rumination, then test the claimed co-occurrence.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: ungulate dental and digestive morphology characters

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species feeding and digestive anatomy accounts

obstacles: Camelids ruminate-like but lack true horns and have different stomachs.
rationale: The traits are standard and extensively recorded for ruminants; joint coding gives a direct, strongly discriminating test.

operationalization: Count rib-bearing vertebrae in snake skeletons across species and compare counts with thirty.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D snake skeletons permitting vertebral and rib counts

obstacles: Paired ribs versus rib-bearing vertebrae must be specified.
rationale: Public skeleton scans make the numerical claim directly observable and allow broad sampling of snake diversity.

operationalization: Code discrete testes in fishes, other gill bearers, snakes and footless vertebrates from reproductive anatomy records.
obstacles: Testes may be diffuse or seasonally inconspicuous.
Ancient testicle may mean external scrotal organ.
rationale: Modern anatomy can distinguish gonads from external testes and directly reveal counterexamples, with broad fish and snake coverage.

operationalization: Measure testis position relative to kidneys and loin in male birds, reptiles, crocodilians and hedgehogs using imaging or dissection records.
obstacles: Season changes organ size and visibility.
“Near the loin” needs a distance criterion.
rationale: Position is directly measurable in the named clades and comparative imaging covers enough taxa for a strong test.

operationalization: Compare testis volume within bird species before and during breeding and estimate fold-change and prevalence across sampled species.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: season- and sex-labelled bird specimens where available

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: bird breeding biology accounts and linked literature

obstacles: Season-labelled gonad measurements are scattered.
“All birds” exceeds available sampling.
rationale: The seasonal prediction is standard and strongly discriminating, but no unified open dataset spans enough bird species to settle universality.

operationalization: Code whether selachian embryos develop from retained yolked eggs and whether birth is live, stratified by reproductive mode and species.
obstacles: Placental viviparity does not fit simple retained-egg terminology.
rationale: Broad shark and ray reproductive datasets directly distinguish oviparity, aplacental viviparity and placental modes, resolving the generalization.

operationalization: Code oviparity and live bearing across snake species and test whether viviparity occurs outside vipers.

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic backbone and occurrence support for species sampling

obstacles: Viper may denote a narrower ancient taxon.
rationale: Reproductive mode is documented across snakes, and many mapped species provide a direct test of the uniqueness claim.

operationalization: Code placental type and visible cotyledons in pregnant ruminants, lagomorphs, rodents and bats, comparing with other viviparous mammals.
obstacles: Cotyledon is used differently in historical and modern placentation.
Pregnant specimens are unevenly available.
rationale: Modern placental classifications test major named groups, but specimen coverage and terminology prevent a complete universal comparison.

operationalization: Trace the aorta and great systemic veins from their proximal origins using vascular imaging and comparative anatomy.
obstacles: “Great vein” must be mapped to vena cava or another vessel.
rationale: Vascular continuity is directly visible in abundant imaging and dissection datasets, clearly distinguishing cardiac from cranial origin.

operationalization: Segment hearts across body sizes, count chambers and model chamber detectability or volume against animal size.
obstacles: Preservation and imaging resolution affect apparent visibility.
rationale: Chamber number and size are direct anatomical measurements, and comparative data can sharply test both the count and size-dependent visibility.

operationalization: Use angiography and histology to determine whether vessels and flowing blood occur within brain tissue across vertebrates.
rationale: Open vascular imaging directly shows intracerebral vessels, producing an immediate and decisive test.

operationalization: Compare clotting time before and after mechanical defibrination or fibrinogen removal, with matched untreated blood.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public experimental repositories that host coagulation datasets and protocols

obstacles: Ancient fibre must be mapped to fibrin or fibrinogen.
Species-specific coagulation differs.
rationale: The intervention and outcome are standard coagulation measurements; existing experimental records and repeatable analyses strongly discriminate the mechanism.

operationalization: Measure fibrinogen and standardized clot strength in deer, roe deer, antelope and hare blood versus matched mammals.
obstacles: No known open harmonized coagulation dataset for all named wildlife.
Handling and anticoagulants strongly affect clotting.
rationale: The comparison is clear, but wildlife coagulation measurements are sparse and not available as a suitable public cross-species dataset.

operationalization: Measure jaw-joint rotation and skull motion during feeding in crocodiles and comparison animals to identify which jaw moves.
obstacles: Whole-head elevation can look like upper-jaw movement.
rationale: Anatomical joint geometry and kinematic evidence separate actual upper-jaw rotation from head movement, giving a decisive test.

operationalization: Compare histology and skeletal composition of dolphin vertebrae with mammalian bone and fish skeletal tissue.
rationale: Dolphin skeletons are widely represented in public collections, and tissue identity is directly observable.

operationalization: Across cranial-appendage-bearing mammals, code solidity, branching, annual shedding and castration status for cervids and noncervids.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: cervid antler growth and shedding accounts

obstacles: Stag may mean red deer rather than all cervids.
Castration evidence is less systematically available.
rationale: The appendage traits and annual cycle are broadly documented, but the castration exception has thinner reusable data.

operationalization: Inspect distal digits of elephants and other toed animals for keratinous nails or hoof-like structures.
obstacles: Whether elephant hoof-like plates count as nails needs a criterion.
rationale: Specimen imaging directly documents elephant toenails and comparative digit coverings, making the anatomical claim decisively testable.

operationalization: Jointly code reproductive mode, limbs and integumentary covering across mammals, reptiles and fishes; search for violations of each universal.
obstacles: Hair, scute and scale homologies require explicit definitions.
rationale: Broad comparative resources cover all three clades and expose counterexamples, although harmonizing ancient categories reduces certainty.

operationalization: Use longitudinal calibrated microscopy of individual hairs to locate pigment loss along shafts and determine whether newly emerged grey hairs begin white.
obstacles: No known open longitudinal hair-level dataset.
Existing hair shafts cannot reveal when each segment changed colour.
rationale: The proposed chronology is measurable, but available images and cross-sectional studies do not provide the longitudinal, follicle-level observations required.

operationalization: Estimate alopecia prevalence by age, sex and castration status, and compare secondary-hair development after prepubertal castration.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: human biology source links are limited but public

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public datasets from alopecia and endocrine studies where deposited

obstacles: Women can have several forms of alopecia.
Historical castration cohorts are rare and selected.
rationale: Large human studies resolve sex and age components, but open data on castration timing and later hair development are scarce.

operationalization: Code age-related plumage colour change across bird species and compare juvenile, adult and senescent common cranes.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: bird life-stage descriptions and linked sources

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic and observation records, some with images

obstacles: Age-labelled plumage observations are not standardized globally.
Moult and season confound age.
rationale: Public observations can identify counterexamples and characterize cranes, but a comprehensive age-controlled colour dataset is lacking.

operationalization: Randomize rams before mating to the candidate water versus control water and compare offspring coat-colour genotypes and phenotypes.
obstacles: No identified public dataset records paternal pre-mating water and lamb colour.
Parental coat-colour genetics is a major confound.
rationale: The causal prediction is experimentally crisp, but existing husbandry data do not contain the exposure and controls; new randomized data are required.

operationalization: Use staged embryo imaging and molecular markers to compare first detectable cardiac blood cells with whole-body tissue differentiation.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: developmental morphology specimens and image series

obstacles: “First” depends on detection method and differentiation definition.
Coverage is concentrated in model vertebrates.
rationale: Developmental series can test selected vertebrates, but stage resolution and broad taxonomic coverage are insufficient for the full scope.

operationalization: Code internal and external viviparity, mammary glands and lactation across mammals, cetaceans, fishes and birds and test their association.
obstacles: Some live-bearing fishes complicate ancient categories.
rationale: The mammalian component is comprehensively documented and comparison groups are well covered, allowing direct tests of both positive and negative clauses.

operationalization: Define thickness by viscosity or total solids, then compare standardized milk measurements for camel, human, donkey and cow.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts linking to milk-composition literature

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public deposited food-composition datasets where available

obstacles: “Thickest” could mean viscosity, fat or total solids.
Lactation stage and processing alter measurements.
rationale: Milk composition data exist for all species, but are scattered and heterogeneous; the result depends materially on the chosen thickness metric.

operationalization: For semen samples, measure sinking or dissolution in standardized water and independently assay fertilization success; compare outcomes blinded.
obstacles: No known public dataset pairs this physical test with fertility.
Water chemistry and semen concentration alter behavior.
rationale: The prediction is direct, but the paired physical and fertility observations needed to assess it are not available as a public dataset.

operationalization: Count arms and sucker rows on specimens across octopus, squid and cuttlefish species, including Eledone.
obstacles: Aristotle’s mollusc category is restricted to cephalopods.
rationale: These conspicuous characters are extensively catalogued and public specimen records can decisively test the universal and exception.

operationalization: Observe mating and inspect male arm morphology to identify hectocotylus use, position, colour and tip shape across octopus species.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: octopus reproductive biology and species accounts

obstacles: Arm numbering conventions differ.
The stated shape may apply only to a mapped species.
rationale: Reproductive behavior and hectocotylized arms are directly documented, permitting a strong test once species and arm numbering are fixed.
